mainText: Hello, Verona! At 2 PM, here is today's balanced dish. We have clear skies at City Hall with a temperature of 49 degrees and the moon in its first quarter. Tonight, you can catch the International Space Station flying over from Mount Horeb toward Madison, reaching high in the sky starting at 5:44 PM.

City business remains active as the Plan Commission prepares for a December 7 meeting to review development projects, including a new site plan for Sub-Zero in the Liberty Business Park. Additionally, residents are reminded that city ordinances and traffic matters are handled through the Municipal Court, where citations can often be managed online or via the police department.
Looking ahead at our local calendar, there are no public events officially scheduled for the next 30 days, so it is a quiet month for community gatherings.

In a noteworthy call from October 23, officers made contact with two juveniles riding eMotos on Ashton Drive; because they had been warned previously, their parents were cited for allowing them to operate the prohibited vehicles.
It is a great day to grab a scoop of Mint Explosion at Culver's. The shop is currently open and will be serving up treats until 10 PM tonight.
